description: Test your knowledge of PA H2 | Approach to Anemia & Lab Investigation.

cards.text: What is the WHO diagnostic cut-off for hemoglobin in non-pregnant adult women?
cards.answer: < 12.0 g/dL. For pregnant women, the cut-off is < 11.0 g/dL (< 10.5 in 2nd trimester).

tip.tip: Remember: 12 for non-pregnant women, 11 for pregnant women

cards.text: How much lower are hemoglobin values in Indian adults compared to Western reference ranges, and what is the recommended field-setting cut-off for non-pregnant women?
cards.answer: Indian adults have Hb values 0.5–1.0 g/dL lower due to nutritional patterns and altitude distribution. Field settings often use 11.0 g/dL as the cut-off for non-pregnant women of reproductive age.

tip.tip: ICMR adjustment: subtract 0.5–1.0 g/dL from WHO thresholds for Indian populations

cards.text: How much does the hemoglobin threshold increase per 1,000 m of altitude?
cards.answer: Approximately 0.2 g/dL per 1,000 m. Residents of high-altitude areas like Leh and Shimla have higher 'normal' Hb than sea-level residents like Chennai.

tip.tip: High altitude = higher normal Hb. Leh (high) > Chennai (sea-level)

cards.text: What does a normal MCV (80–100 fL) with elevated RDW suggest, and what should you look for on the blood smear?
cards.answer: Elevated RDW with normal MCV suggests a mixed deficiency (e.g., iron + B12 deficiency). The smear will show a dimorphic population with anisocytosis.

tip.tip: High RDW = anisocytosis. Normal MCV + high RDW = think MIXED deficiency

cards.text: Name the three major etiological categories of anemia.
cards.answer: 1) Decreased production (hypoproliferative) — marrow failure; 2) Increased destruction (hemolytic) — RBC breakdown; 3) Blood loss — external hemorrhage.

cards.text: List four causes of decreased RBC production (hypoproliferative anemia).
cards.answer: Nutritional deficiency (iron, B12, folate), bone marrow failure (aplasia, infiltration), anemia of chronic disease, and renal failure (EPO deficiency).

cards.text: Differentiate between megaloblastic and non-megaloblastic macrocytic anemia.
cards.answer: Megaloblastic (B12/folate deficiency): hypersegmented neutrophils on smear, impaired DNA synthesis. Non-megaloblastic (liver disease, hypothyroidism, alcohol): normal neutrophil morphology, no nuclear maturation defect.

tip.tip: Mega = hypersegmented neutrophils. Non-mega = normal neutrophils

cards.text: Why is it important to interpret hemoglobin alongside clinical volume status (e.g., hydration state)?
cards.answer: Hemoglobin and hematocrit reflect RBC concentration, not absolute mass. Dehydration causes hemoconcentration masking anemia; IV fluids and splenomegaly cause dilutional pseudoanemia with normal RBC mass.

tip.tip: Hb is concentration. Assess volume status: dehydration hides anemia, fluid loading hides it.
